title: Rocket Supply
tags: place value,hundreds,tens and ones,three-digit numbers,expanded form,number names,skip counting,count by 5,count by 10,count by 100,compare numbers,greater than,less than,add,subtract,regrouping,within 100,within 1000,second grade,grade 2,math,maths,3d,space,rocket,read aloud,learning
description: Stock the rocket on the space base launch pad! A flat pallet is a hundred, a rack is a ten and a canister is a one. Load the right number, read a load, count by fives, tens and hundreds along the fuel gauge, pick the sign between two numbers, and add and take away with tens and ones. When the load is right, the rocket lifts off. Every instruction is read aloud, so new readers can play too.
notes: Number Quest Launchpad Unit 5, The Hundreds Hedge (grade 2): a Kit 2 game on Oomba3D 1.1.0 in the Space Base theme 1.0.0 (the theme's own dark sky, ink outlines, gear button, graphics 'auto'), loaded with exactly kit2ImportMap() (tests/unit/rocket-supply.test.js checks the literal map). The base (domes, tunnels, garage, towers, wind turbines, sun panels, pads with landers, rovers, cargo, rocks, craters and the hills at the edge of the plain) is the theme's own pieces on the game's red ground, under the game's own stars and a ringed blue world; the library's soft clouds are sent below the ground. The loading pad, the launch lift, the rocket, the fuel gauge, the number boards and the supply pods are the game's own simple meshes. One yellow canister is a ONE; a blue rack of ten canisters is a TEN; a flat green pallet, ten by ten, is a HUNDRED. A load stands on a pad with a bay for each place (named 100s, 10s and 1s on its front edge): pallets in one pile with a gap after five, racks side by side in fives, canisters in stacks of five, so each place can be counted and an empty place is seen to be empty. Made for a child who is only starting to read: every instruction is short, shown and spoken through BRB.speak (voice role friendly; the speaker button says it again), numbers are big, and every answer is a big button. No timer, no lives, no fail state: a wrong answer wobbles the button and rocks the rocket (a dashed outline on the button with reduced motion), shows why on the pad and gets a spoken hint; then another try. When a round is right the rocket lifts off at once (no countdown) and a new one comes down for the next round. Three chapters of six rounds, made by window.RocketSupply.round(chapter, n, lap) (the block between /* rocket-supply:begin */ and /* rocket-supply:end */, pure, seeded from the round number; a replay lap gets new numbers). build (step 5.1; 2.NBT.A.1, 2.NBT.A.3): 1 load a three-digit number with 'Load a hundred', 'Load a ten', 'Load a one', 'Take one off' and 'Lift off' (the chip shows the load so far in expanded form, 200 + 30 + 2; ten canisters lock into a rack and ten racks into a pallet, said as it happens); 2 no pallets today: load 110 to 140 with racks of ten, and the tenth rack locks the ten into a pallet ('10 tens make 1 hundred'); 3 read a load with an empty place and pick its number from three (407, with 47 and 470 offered; on odd laps 470); 4 read a load of three different digits (the digits swapped are offered); 5 a number from its parts, with the value of each place on a board over it (300 + 40 + 2; on odd laps 500 + 6 or 500 + 60); 6 a number from its name, heard and written in words on the chip ('two hundred seventeen', with 207 and 270 offered; on odd laps a name such as 'six hundred forty-seven'). A wrong pick shows how many stand in each place. count (5.2; 2.NBT.A.2, 2.NBT.A.4): 1-3 what comes next, counting by fives, by tens and by hundreds along the fuel gauge (a pipe with a lamp and a number at each mark; the fuel has run as far as the last number counted; on odd laps the tens and hundreds start off a round number: 234, 244, 254); the wrong numbers are one more, or a hop of the wrong size; a wrong pick shows the hop between the marks; 4-6 the sign between two three-digit numbers, >, = or <, said as 'is greater than', 'is equal to', 'is less than' with the reason ('7 hundreds is more than 5 hundreds'): the hundreds differ (and the smaller number has the bigger tens and ones), the same digits in another order, the same hundreds and tens; other laps bring the same hundreds, and the same number twice. The two loads stand side by side on a wide screen and one above the other on a tall one; a wrong pick marks the place that decides. fuel (5.3; 2.NBT.B.5, also 2.OA.B.2): 1 a quick adding fact past ten (6 + 8); 2 two two-digit numbers whose ones make a new ten (38 + 17); 3 taking away where a ten must be opened (67 − 19); 4 a quick taking-away fact past ten (12 − 3); 5 adding again (on odd laps the ones make ten exactly, 46 + 34); 6 taking away again (on odd laps from a round ten, 70 − 26). The numbers stand as racks and canisters; three number buttons, the wrong ones a real mistake (the new ten forgotten, a ten too many, the smaller digit taken from the bigger). The work is shown on the pad when the answer is right, or after a wrong pick: the ones come together and ten of them lock into a new rack, or a rack opens into ten canisters and what is taken away stays as a pale outline. Totals stay within 100. The player picks one of the theme's five adventurers as a helper; the helper stands on the launch lift beside the rocket (never in front of a pod or a number) and cheers at lift-off. The lift stands beside the pad on a wide screen and behind it, raised, on a tall one. Lesson mode: BRB.params { chapter: build | count | fuel, lock: 1 } opens that chapter only; finishing its six rounds calls BRB.gameOver({ won: true }) once (the single call site), which completes the course step. With no parameters a picture menu offers the three chapters. Save: BRB.storage 'rocket-supply-v1' holds only which chapters are finished. Every step of a round (pods landing, the sum being worked, the fuel running on, the lift-off, the pause) is run by the game loop, not by wall-clock timers. Layout: the camera backs off until the pad, the load and the rocket fit between the words and the buttons, with room kept over the buttons for a hint. Keyboard: every answer is a button (Tab, Enter, Space). A device without WebGL2 or import maps gets the site's 'needs a newer device' card. Words: English only (the I18N block, read by server/services/tts-lines.js for AI voices). Test handle: window.__rs (also window.__brbTest): state(), fast(), hero(id), act('answer', v), act('load', 'h' | 't' | 'o'), act('off'), act('go'), spot(), heroAt().
